prompt: For a 2-input AND gate, the output Y is 1 when…

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: AND is logical multiplication — Y = A · B. Picture a series circuit: current flows only when both switches are closed.

prompt: A 2-input OR gate produces Y = 0 only when…

steps.body: OR is logical addition — Y = A + B. Parallel switches: current flows if any path is closed.

prompt: A 2-input NAND gate has A = 1 and B = 1. What is Y?

prompt: A 2-input NOR gate has A = 0 and B = 0. What is Y?

steps.title: Result
steps.body: NOR outputs 1 only when both inputs are 0.

prompt: The output of a 2-input XOR gate is 1 when…

steps.title: Definition
steps.body: XOR (exclusive OR) outputs 1 only when the inputs are not equal.

steps.title: Pattern
steps.body: Rows 01 and 10 produce 1 — both are cases where inputs differ.

prompt: A 2-input XNOR gate outputs 1 when…

steps.title: XNOR is inverted XOR
steps.body: XNOR flips every row of the XOR truth table.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: Output is 1 exactly when the inputs are equal — 00 or 11.

prompt: Why is NAND called a universal gate?

steps.body: A gate is universal if AND, OR, and NOT can all be built from it.

steps.title: NAND build
steps.body: Tie inputs for NOT; NAND-then-NOT for AND; NOT-both-then-NAND for OR.

steps.title: Answer
steps.body: NAND can implement every Boolean function alone.
